profile.purpose: A four-year review of the Wolverine Original 1000 Mile Boot, asking whether it is a good first Goodyear-welted boot. It covers sizing, wear, leather, sole, construction and style, and compares it with the Red Wing Iron Ranger and Thursday Boots.
profile.thesis: After four years of occasional wear, the creator assesses the Wolverine 1000 Mile as an entry-level heritage boot. He weighs its Horween Chromexcel leather, US manufacture, cork midsole and resoleable welt against its slick leather sole, mid-grade leather and cosmetic quality-control flaws.
key_takeaways: Covers sizing: he went true to his boot size (8D) and discusses whether a half size up suits thick wool socks.
Explains Horween Chromexcel leather: pull-up, history, tanning process, and that Wolverine uses a mid grade.
Discusses the leather outsole's lack of traction, gravel pitting, the stacked leather and rubber heel, and the idea of having a cobbler add a Vibram sole.
Describes the cork midsole, break-in, triple stitching, Goodyear welt resoleability and the boot's weight.
Discusses quality-control issues such as loose threads and odd creasing, which he sees as cosmetic.
Positions the boot as a dressier basic boot rather than a modern work boot, and gives styling ideas.
Compares it with the Red Wing Iron Ranger and Thursday Boots on price, leather, heritage and style.

outline.title: Introduction
outline.summary: A no-music intro filmed at his old elementary school, framing the question of how tough the boots are.

outline.title: The backstory
outline.summary: How he chose between Red Wing Iron Rangers and Wolverine 1000 Miles about four years ago, and won the Wolverines in a contest.

outline.title: Acquisition and details
outline.summary: Context on how much he has actually worn them, the aftermarket leather laces, and the boot's place as a popular entry-level Goodyear-welted boot. The filming moves to New York.

outline.title: Sizing and fit
outline.summary: He went true to size (8D) against advice to size up, and discusses fit with thin cotton versus thick wool socks. He recommends trying them on in person.

outline.title: Wear and durability
outline.summary: How the boots held up through a week of snow and slush at Sundance, and a scratch from a stiletto heel. Chromexcel pull-up lets scratches be buffed out.

outline.title: Leather quality and origin
outline.summary: The history of Horween and Chromexcel, including use on war-era tanks, and its tanning process. Wolverine uses a mid grade of leather, with loose grain creasing. Both leather and construction are US-made.

outline.title: Sole and outsole issues
outline.summary: The leather outsole has almost no traction and gets pitted by gravel, and he would like a rubber Vibram-type sole added. The heel is stacked leather with rubber.

outline.title: Construction and comfort
outline.summary: The cork midsole molds to the foot, so break-in is manageable and comfort is good afterwards. Triple stitching on the vamp adds durability.

outline.title: Quality control and style
outline.summary: Loose threads and creasing are cosmetic QC issues. The boots are heavy and stiff when new, more professor or desk-job than construction boot, dressier than Iron Rangers, and resoleable thanks to the Goodyear welt.

outline.title: Conclusion and comparison
outline.summary: Summary and styling with jeans and leather laces. He asks why the 1000 Mile has a cult following compared with Red Wing Iron Rangers, and compares it with Thursday Boots on price and heritage.
